description:
FOUND s498c (Opus, 2026-09-26), member 0's blocked-mask variant.
Reproducer: `perl -MPOSIX -e 'POSIX::sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, POSIX::SigSet->new(SIGUSR1)); exec @ARGV' -- perl -e '$|=1; $SIG{USR1} = sub { print "caught\n" }; kill USR1 => $$; print "end\n"'` prints `end` (the signal stays pending); the same under ./runpcl prints `caught` then `end`.
Cause: sb-kernel:signal-cold-init-or-reinit ends by UNBLOCKING every signal (it undoes the C runtime's block_blockable_signals).  The #2263 capture point (the encapsulation of that function) could also record the inherited mask and re-block it after SBCL's start-up, excluding the signals SBCL needs (the deny list; SIGURG for interrupt-thread).  Rare in practice (a parent that execs with signals blocked); not-supported "%SIG" names it.
subject: EDGE: an inherited BLOCKED signal mask is cleared at SBCL start-up; perl keeps it (a blocked USR1 never runs perl's handler, PCL runs it)
